objective: Threat and data-exposure detection: Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie

sources.cite: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide: Design secure architectures 30%, Design resilient architectures 26%, Design high-performing architectures 24%, Design cost-optimized architectures 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the exam guide PDF on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: Task 1.2, knowledge of 'Security services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Cognito, Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Macie)'.

sources.cite: Amazon GuardDuty User Guide: Remediating a potentially compromised Amazon EC2 instance
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: create a dedicated Isolation security group with no rule for 0.0.0.0/0, associate it and remove all other security groups; 'The existing tracked connections won't be terminated as a result of changing security groups - only future traffic will be effectively blocked'; identify and stop the source of the activity (closing ports, changing access policies, upgrading applications).

sources.cite: AWS re:Post Knowledge Center: How do I resolve GuardDuty credential alerts (InstanceCredentialExfiltration)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: the temporary credentials were created on an EC2 instance in your environment and used by an outside host; deny the role's permissions with an explicit Deny conditioned on the role ID and session; 'Remediate a potentially compromised EC2 instance'; use the instance metadata service securely.

sources.cite: AWS IAM User Guide: Revoke IAM role temporary security credentials
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: Revoke active sessions attaches the inline policy AWSRevokeOlderSessions, which 'denies all access to users who assumed the role in the past'; 'If the user assumes the role after you revoked the permissions, then the deny policy does not apply to that user'; the condition uses aws:TokenIssueTime. The page does not say how instance profiles pick up new credentials, so the scenario does not model an outage from the revocation.

sources.cite: Amazon Macie User Guide: Types of Macie findings
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: Macie generates 'policy findings and sensitive data findings'; SensitiveData:S3Object/Financial: 'The object contains sensitive financial information, such as bank account numbers or credit card numbers'; Policy:IAMUser/S3BucketPublic for buckets opened to anonymous users.

sources.cite: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0, recommendation 6.7 'Ensure that the EC2 Metadata Service only allows IMDSv2' (to verify)
sources.note: Only the recommendation's title was seen, in a search result on 2026-11-16; the benchmark text and the EC2 documentation on IMDSv2 were not read. That requiring IMDSv2 blocks metadata theft through a simple server-side request forgery (which cannot send the PUT for a session token) is the author's summary, to verify.
Fictional company. Addresses use the documentation range 203.0.113.0/24 (IETF RFC 5737). The object counts and times are the author's.

brief.situation: You are the solutions architect on call for Larkfield Travel, a fictional agency. At 14:00 GuardDuty raises a high-severity finding: credentials of web-app-role, the role of the web tier's instances, are being used from an address outside AWS. Macie runs automated sensitive data discovery on the account's buckets.
handover: The web tier is an Application Load Balancer and four instances in an Auto Scaling group, all with web-app-role.
web-app-role can read the bucket of customer exports and the product images bucket.
howItWorks: The board shows detection, the web tier, the role and the data, and updates as you work.
Each task takes your time: start it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
When you close the incident, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The attacker copies about 200 objects every 5 minutes while it holds working credentials.

How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. finance-2019.csv is the 1,800th object in the attacker's listing: about 30 minutes of uninterrupted copying.

How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. Twenty-five minutes after a revocation, the attacker fetches fresh role credentials through the same request forgery if it is still open.

trail.label: Trace how the credentials left: web logs and the instance's requests to the metadata service
trail.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.log: The /preview?url= feature fetches any URL server-side; requests for http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ came through the load balancer. Instances allow IMDSv1.

effects.finding: A server-side request forgery reads the role's credentials from the metadata service through any web instance, not only i-web-03.

revoke.label: Revoke the role's active sessions
revoke.why: No active attacker session to revoke.

effects.log: AWSRevokeOlderSessions attached: every session issued before now is denied, including the attacker's.

writeup.question: For the record: what GuardDuty and Macie told you, how you stopped the attacker, and why it will not come back.

parts.label: Detection
parts.criteria: Uses GuardDuty for the credential misuse and Macie for which data is at risk.
parts.modelAnswer: GuardDuty's InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS finding showed web-app-role credentials used from 203.0.113.80 against lark-exports; Macie showed that bucket holds card numbers, so stopping the copying came first.

parts.label: Stop
parts.criteria: Revokes the role's sessions and closes the way the credentials were taken before they can be taken again.
parts.modelAnswer: Revoking active sessions denied every session issued before then; the /preview request forgery read credentials from the metadata service, so I required IMDSv2 (and turned off /preview) before the attacker could get new ones.

parts.label: Preserve and report
parts.criteria: Keeps the instance for investigation (isolate and snapshot, not terminate) and hands privacy the CloudTrail object list.
parts.modelAnswer: i-web-03 is isolated with a snapshot rather than terminated; privacy and legal have the list of copied objects.

expertPath.text: GuardDuty: web-app-role credentials used from outside AWS against lark-exports. Macie: that bucket holds card numbers.
Revoke the role's active sessions; trace the /preview request forgery to the metadata service; require IMDSv2 everywhere.
Isolate and snapshot i-web-03; give privacy the copied-object list from CloudTrail.

contained.headline: Good: out, and kept out
contained.body: GuardDuty showed whose credentials and Macie showed what was at stake. Revoking sessions stopped the copying, and requiring IMDSv2 closed the way they were taken before the attacker could take new ones. The instance stays as evidence.

gaps.headline: Stopped, with gaps
gaps.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what was left: the instance, the root cause before re-theft, the report to privacy, or the lesson.

cardsOut.headline: The card file left
cardsOut.body: Macie pointed at the card data and GuardDuty at the credentials from the first minutes. Revoking the role's sessions was a five-minute step.

stillActive.headline: Still inside
stillActive.body: A revocation denies only sessions issued before it. With the request forgery open, the attacker simply took new credentials.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: GuardDuty's InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS finding shows web-app-role credentials from i-web-03 used by 203.0.113.80 to copy lark-exports, and Macie shows that bucket holds card numbers, so stop the copying first: revoke the role's active sessions, which denies every session issued before then. The credentials were read from the metadata service through the /preview request forgery, which works through any web instance, so require IMDSv2 on every instance and the launch template (and turn off /preview) before the attacker takes fresh credentials. Isolate and snapshot i-web-03 rather than terminating it, do not archive the finding, and give privacy and legal the copied-object list from CloudTrail.
